key_insight: An XGBoost model using clinical and ECG-related features predicted pacing-induced cardiomyopathy in AV block patients with moderately good discrimination.
clinical_relevance: This could help identify higher-risk patients before or after pacemaker implantation and support more individualized pacing strategy selection.
method: 125 pacemaker recipients with AV block and HFmrEF/HFpEF
Compared logistic regression, SVM, random forest, and XGBoost with stratified 4-fold cross-validation
evidence_signal: In 125 patients followed a median of 4.8 years, PICM occurred in 32.8% and XGBoost achieved AUROC 0.831 with sensitivity 0.805 and specificity 0.845.
watch_item: The model was developed in a relatively small cohort, so external validation and calibration in independent populations are still needed before routine use.
paper_title: Machine Learning-based Prediction of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Underlying Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
